reasoning_traces.think:
The core duality lies between mnemonization and perception as distinct pathways for sign-gestalt formation. Mnemonization operates via prior fusion structures, wherein partial sign stimuli activate expectations for the whole gestalt through associative memory. Perception, conversely, arises from simultaneous presentation of all gestalt components, enabling direct holistic expectation formation. Both processes instantiate a shared mathematical object: the gestalt expectation function E(G), which maps sensory inputs I to expectation states S. For mnemonization, E(G) = f(I_s, F_{prev}), where I_s is the sign component and F_{prev} denotes prior fusions. For perception, E(G) = g(I_{all}), where I_{all} represents all gestalt components. The failure mode of each lies in structural mismatch: mnemonization fails when prior fusions are insufficient or corrupted, while perception fails when component stimuli lack coherence or are incomplete. These dual mechanisms define a dynamic system with two operational regimes: associative recall (mnemonization) and pattern recognition (perception). Their interplay determines cognitive efficiency and adaptability in complex environments.
